All of the workshop's **core materials in one place.** Each **module** pairs **1:1:1:1** across four layers — a slide-deck **lecture**, a long-form **book chapter** (reading), a hands-on **laptop tutorial** (on `ifnb`), and the matching **Talapas HPC script** (the same `ifnb` analysis as a SLURM batch job). Click straight through to any of them. Material *beyond* the workshop — prerequisite appendices, external papers, the from-raw-FASTQs pipeline — lives under [Additional Resources](Additional_Resources.qmd).

## What's in each layer

- **Lecture** — the slide deck (reveal.js); the in-class summary of the topic.
- **Reading (chapter)** — the long-form prose "textbook" treatment, with worked examples and cross-references to the prerequisite [appendices](Resources_Folder/Reference_Material.html).
- **Tutorial** — a hands-on, downloadable `.qmd` you open in RStudio and run chunk by chunk, with *Think about it* prompts and collapsible answers. The laptop tutorials run on the laptop-friendly **`ifnb`** dataset.
- **Talapas script** — the *same* tutorial workflow as a streamlined R script you submit to UO's **Talapas** HPC cluster as a SLURM job. Each script is numbered to match its tutorial.

::: callout-tip
**Recommended order.** Watch the lecture and read the chapter *before* working the matching tutorial: the lecture is the summary, the chapter is the detail, the tutorial is the runnable code, and the Talapas script scales it on the cluster.
:::

## Download the tutorials

Each tutorial is a downloadable `.qmd` with code, prompts, and collapsible answers — open it in RStudio, point the data paths at your local copy (see [Datasets](Datasets.qmd)), and run it chunk by chunk.

::: callout-important
Downloads serve each file as `Tutorial_XX_….qmd.txt`. After saving, **drop the trailing `.txt`** so the name ends in `.qmd`, then open it in RStudio. (The `.txt` suffix stops the browser from rendering the source as a webpage.)

## The Talapas HPC track

The fourth leg of each module: the same `ifnb` analysis as **streamlined R scripts** you submit to Talapas as SLURM jobs — no raw FASTQs and no new dataset (script 01 loads `ifnb` straight from Bioconductor). Start with [Talapas 01 — SLURM Basics](Exercise_Folder/Talapas/Tutorial_Talapas_01_SLURM_Basics.html), then the [Talapas 03 — Analysis Pipeline](Exercise_Folder/Talapas/Tutorial_Talapas_03_Analysis_Pipeline.html) overview, which ties the scripts together and lists the submission commands. Submit each with the generic wrapper <a href="Exercise_Folder/Talapas/scripts/run_rscript.sbatch" download>run_rscript.sbatch</a> (e.g. `sbatch run_rscript.sbatch 01_qc_preprocessing.R`).

**Core pipeline** (run in order — each script reads the `.rds` the previous one wrote):

| Script | Parallels module | Download |
|---|---|---|

:::

## Datasets

The laptop tutorials and the Talapas track both run on **`ifnb`** (Kang *et al.* 2017; \~14k PBMCs, CTRL + IFN-β, \~25 MB); Tutorial 11 adds **`stxBrain`** (10x Visium mouse brain), and the bonus tutorials (09 scATAC, 10 WGCNA) have their own datasets. Full download URLs, the expected directory layout, and a disk-space budget are on the **[Datasets](Datasets.qmd)** page.
